sections.markdown:
## Work zones, road rules, restraints and phones

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Use high beams only in rural surroundings when other vehicles are not nearby. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Headlights are required beginning half an hour after sunset through half an hour before sunrise, whenever it rains, and whenever visibility is limited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Dim the headlights within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle and when following another vehicle within 200 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
Use low beams on illuminated roads, in rain, fog, snow or smoke, and when the visible distance falls below 200 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
Keep headlight lenses clean, make sure the lamps work, and periodically have their aim checked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A01
At night, choose a speed that permits stopping within the road distance your headlights illuminate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A01
Slow at night when approaching a curve or oncoming traffic. With greatly reduced visibility, use the edge line as a lane guide, or the centerline if no edge line is present. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A01
For night driving, keep the windshield clean and look carefully for signs, pedestrians and vehicles stopped along the road's edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A01
Do not continue driving when tired, and do not stop on the roadway at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A01
Each front-seat occupant of a passenger vehicle must use the lap-and-shoulder belt. All passenger-vehicle occupants younger than 18 must use a safety belt wherever seated. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes Georgia's belt law as primary enforcement, allowing an officer to stop and cite a belt violation without first seeing another offense. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A01
Correct belt use helps retain the occupant in the vehicle, distribute crash force over stronger body areas, and prevent contact with the interior or other occupants. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A01
A driver carrying a child younger than 8 ordinarily must use an approved child restraint matched to the child's height and weight. The handbook excludes taxis and public transit and notes additional limited exemptions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A01
Distracted driving diverts attention from operating the vehicle. The handbook's examples include phone use, reading, eating, grooming, navigation-device use and adjusting audio; passengers and animals can also distract. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A01
Georgia's described due-care rule prohibits activities that distract from safe vehicle operation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A01
Unless on official business, do not follow a responding fire vehicle or other emergency vehicle closer than 200 feet, and do not park within 500 feet of fire apparatus stopped for an alarm. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A01
When litter is thrown, dropped or deposited from a motor vehicle, the handbook assigns responsibility to the vehicle's operator. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A01
The litter-control prohibition covers discarding waste on public or private property and in the state's waters; discarded materials and rubbish fall within the stated definition. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=25]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A02
The handbook's hands-free rule prohibits holding or supporting a phone or standalone electronic device with any part of the body while operating on a highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A02
The described hands-free arrangements use a mounted holder, wireless equipment or headphones; a device that impairs hearing remains separately prohibited by the handbook's hearing rule. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A02
The hands-free section prohibits writing, reading or sending text communications, including messages, email and internet data, while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A02
The hands-free section also prohibits watching, recording or broadcasting a movie or video while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A02
Approach a flashing-light postal-service vehicle or a vehicle with active sanitation workers cautiously. Unless an officer directs otherwise, change into a lane not beside it when safety and traffic allow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A02
If changing lanes for a covered postal or sanitation vehicle is impossible, unlawful or unsafe, reduce to a reasonable speed for conditions and prepare to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=26]

Misconceptions: Hands-free equipment does not authorize distracted driving or equipment that impairs hearing; an advisory speed and a regulatory limit have different roles.
Mnemonic: Slow, observe, give room, follow directions.
Glossary: An advisory speed is guidance for the particular warned condition; a controlled-access roadway has designated entrances and exits.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Penalty schedules, toll interoperability, restraint exemptions and incomplete statutory summaries remain current-official-source review.

verification_debt.claim_text: The dated handbook facts retain source freshness, rights and independent factual-review debt; no current-law equivalence or live service/fee policy is certified.
Work-zone fatality statistics and historical worker totals are not verified current and are withheld.

Work-zone, impairment, reckless/aggressive/stunt-driving, litter and phone fines, jail terms, points, suspension durations, restoration charges and limited-permit schedules are withheld pending current legal confirmation.
Blood-alcohol numeric clauses on this page use a mass expression without a complete concentration unit; no percentage is inferred here. The later impairment section must be read separately.
Toll-pass registration, reciprocity and violation notices are changing service policy and withheld pending current issuer evidence.
The child-restraint summary notes additional exemptions without enumerating them. This is an incomplete handbook summary; no exhaustive current exemption list is asserted.
The hands-free summary does not enumerate every statutory exception; current exceptions and applicability require official verification.
The postal/sanitation fallback-speed comparison uses the same awkward fixed-speed/reduction wording as the bicycle rule. Its exact numeric comparison is withheld pending authoritative clarification.
Work-zone sign drawings are not reproduced or treated as image-recognition evidence.
